newsitem.title: INDIA: India should permit hedging of oil imports - panel.
newsitem.headline: India should permit hedging of oil imports - panel.

text.p: A parliamentary committee on Wednesday said Indian Oil Corp (IOC) was using outdated purchasing methods and urged the government to permit state firms to use risk management techniques such as hedging.
The committee said in a report to parliament that IOC was buying crude oil and petroleum products through annual contracts and tenders instead of hedging risk to save money.
The committee said it was "shocked" to find that IOC, the sole crude oil purchasing agency, had not taken preliminary steps in risk management in its imports despite highly volatile world prices.
But IOC said its hands were tied.
"We have not been indulging in hedging so far because it has not been approved by the government or the empowered standing committee," an IOC spokesman told Reuters.
The parliamentary committee, headed by Congress party deputy A.R. Antulay and comprising 45 deputies, is an advisory one and its recommendations are not binding.

The report said Petroleum Ministry officials had told the committee that risk managment techniques had not been used because existing policies do not permit participation in forward, futures and over-the-counter markets.
"We have to change the entire procedure," the report quoted Petroleum Secretary Vijay Kelkar as telling the committee.
The committee said it was told that IOC had appointed an international consultant to review and guide its international trading activities.
But the report said the committee had reasons to believe the selection of the consultant "was done in an ad hoc manner without following proper procedure and therefore it lacked transparency".
It said the committee doubted if the Petroleum Ministry and IOC had properly analysed the offers of seven consultants who had made presentations.
The committee recommended that the choice of the consultant be put on hold while the offers by the six other experts are reexamined.
IOC officials said they had not yet received the report. "We are yet to receive the report and would respond to the committee's observations thereafter," the IOC spokesman said.
Petroleum Ministry officials were unavailable for comment.
